assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with additional cardiovascular and renal benefit. The work links gut-hormone physiology to a major new drug class, with clear originality and very large patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (gut physiology and the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and the proglucagon and GLP-2 work) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) are the most defensible three. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's industrial drug development is important but sits on the translational side, and the allocation among basic and translational contributors is the hard question. As I recall it, the Mojsov priority question is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy has been confirmed repeatedly in large independent trials, and the mechanism is well understood. Recognition is timely, since the impact is at its peak.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among the basic discoverers and the industrial developers is contested.
I have not independently verified the details of the credit dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation, and that blocking it benefits patients, established the principle of cytokine-targeted therapy in chronic autoimmune disease. The discovery is clear and original, and its impact has been broad across rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are a natural pair, linked by the concept and by the first proof-of-concept clinical trials. A third place could be argued for others in TNF biology or antibody engineering, but the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Anti-TNF biologics have been used for more than two decades, with strong independent confirmation, and the field is stable. Recognition is mature and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the prize as primarily clinical translation rather than basic discovery.
The TNF biology itself involves earlier contributors not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. This is a conceptually new therapeutic modality, supported by approved products and a clear line from discovery to cure in some patients.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June are the clearest leaders in chimeric receptor design and clinical proof. Rosenberg contributed foundational adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other early designers of chimeric receptors are not in the supplied names, so the credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several products are approved, with long-term follow-up in leukemia and lymphoma. Limits remain in solid tumours, toxicity and cost, but the core finding is established.
uncertainties: Early chimeric-receptor inventors outside the supplied names may need recognition.
Long-term durability and safety data are still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived self-organizing organoids from single adult Lgr5-positive stem cells created a general platform for studying tissue renewal, disease modelling, host-pathogen interactions and personalized drug testing. It is original and has been widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell identity and the organoid concept, and Sato was the first author of the pivotal intestinal organoid culture work. This is a compact and fair two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: The method has been reproduced in many independent laboratories. Therapeutic and diagnostic impact is still developing, so the case rests mainly on a research-enabling tool.
uncertainties: Overlap with stem-cell culture precedents may raise credit questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision and has changed how circuits and behaviour are studied. The impact on basic neurobiology is large, and clinical uses are emerging, for example in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted approach) are separate contributions. With six credited names a prize of at most three is difficult to configure fairly, and any trio will leave out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely confirmed and stable, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Attribution is highly contested and cannot be resolved by a three-person limit.
The value is mostly as a research tool, with limited therapeutic use so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The orexin/hypocretin system explains narcolepsy type 1 and gave a defined molecular basis for sleep-wake regulation. The result links physiology, genetics and disease, and led to orexin-receptor antagonists and agonists in development.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa identified orexin and its receptors, de Lecea and Kilduff independently found hypocretin, and Mignot's canine genetics and human work established the narcolepsy link. The overlap in discovery is a real attribution problem, and a trio will omit one of two groups.
assessment.maturity: The orexin loss in narcolepsy has been replicated, and drug approvals for insomnia support the pathway. Orexin agonists are still in trials.
uncertainties: Credit is split between independent discoveries of the same peptide.
Therapeutic validation of agonists is not complete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data show large reductions in cervical cancer. It is a rare case of a vaccine that directly prevents cancer, with global public health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 particle approach, and Frazer contributed to the VLP work and to the vaccine's development with Zhou. Other groups made parallel contributions, and the supplied three names are a plausible but not undisputed set.
assessment.maturity: National programmes now show cervical-cancer incidence falling in vaccinated cohorts, which gives strong independent confirmation. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Parallel work by other groups, including the Zhou contribution, could affect credit.
I have not independently verified the details of the competing priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of IL-6, its receptor and its signalling, and the demonstration that IL-6 receptor blockade treats rheumatoid arthritis, Castleman disease and cytokine release syndrome, represent a clear bench-to-bedside cytokine story that has reached many patients.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano cloned IL-6 and described the receptor and signalling, and Kishimoto led the therapeutic antibody effort. The two-person configuration is coherent, though the therapeutic arm may involve others.
assessment.maturity: Tocilizumab has been used clinically for years and its mechanism is well established, with confirmation in COVID-19 and cytokine release syndrome. Recognition is mature, but the case overlaps with TNF in the same clinical area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the anti-TNF case, so both together would crowd one therapeutic area.
Contributions of early cytokine researchers outside the supplied names are unclear.
